terminal.open: Show the commands this task ran

terminal.refusal.closed: The session is not running. Open it again.

model.remote.keyChecking: Checking the Keychain for a key…
model.remote.noConsent: Settings → Privacy → Allow remote providers is off, so a prompt is refused rather than answered on this machine. Nothing leaves the app until that switch is on.
model.remote.notConfigured: The provider has no address and model yet. Set both in Settings → Model → Remote provider.
model.remote.noKey: No key is saved in the macOS Keychain, so the provider would refuse the next prompt. Paste one in Settings → Model.

model.free.title: Free model
model.free.noService: This model is served by the free-model service on this Mac, and that service is not answering, so nothing can be asked of it yet. Open the FreeCode app — every free row goes live when it does, and no key is involved.
composer.placeholder: Describe a task for the model you picked
composer.approve.auto_approve: Reads, workspace edits and — while Terminal access is on — a command run on their own; a web call runs only while the Privacy switch is on. Anything with other side effects stops and asks you first.
composer.approve.ask_always: Reads run on their own. Every write, every command and every web call stops and asks you first.
composer.approve.plan_only: The run explores with read-only tools and answers with a plan: writes, commands and web calls are refused.
composer.approve.custom: Each call is decided by its own row in Settings, not by this dial.
composer.agent.on: Every prompt runs as an agent: the model may read this workspace, make a file in it and change one, and each round it asks costs the context window one tool result. What it may change without asking is the approval dial's answer, and nothing else reaches past this machine except, while the privacy switch is on, a Wikipedia search and one page read.
composer.agent.onShell: Every prompt runs as an agent, and Terminal access is on: the model may read this workspace, make a file in it, change one, and run one command there with your own permissions. Each round it asks costs the context window one tool result. What it may change without asking is the approval dial's answer.
composer.agent.subagents: Subagents is on: one of the rounds may hand a self-contained question to a second local model run that can only read this workspace, and its answer comes back as one tool result.
composer.agent.proseRoute: A free model is selected: FreeCode answers the run on this Mac, working in the project folder you picked, and the writes appear here as rows and a diff like a local run's. One thing that route cannot give: Revert holds no copy of the file from before the change, so a page it wrote stays written until you undo it yourself.
composer.picture.failed: That file could not be read as a picture, so nothing was attached.
composer.review.open: Show which lines this run changed
composer.review.close: Hide which lines this run changed

modelPicker.freeNote: The next prompt is answered by the free model picked here, through the free-model service on this Mac — which is not answering now, so no free row can be picked until it is.

settings.row.projectRoot.desc: The folder an agent run reads, writes, and runs the project's tests, build and linter in — and the folder its git reads report. Empty works in the folder this build resolves for itself. A chosen folder that has since moved refuses the run by name rather than falling back.
settings.row.projectRoot.chooseTitle: Choose the folder runs work in
settings.row.approvalMode.desc: The mode the next run is built with. Auto approve runs reads, workspace edits and — while Terminal access is on — a command on its own, and web calls only while the Privacy switch is on; Ask answers reads the same way and stops at every change. Either way, a call the mode cannot settle appears as a card over the composer, and the run waits there for as long as the Command and approval timeout below allows.
settings.row.shellEnabled.desc: Off by default. While it is on, the model may run a command with your own user's permissions: it starts in the workspace but is not confined to it, and it can reach the network even while the Privacy switch is off. The same switch admits the project's own tests, build and linter, which run code the workspace already carries. Every command that runs appears in the transcript.
settings.row.shellTimeout.desc: The one number two waits read. A command still running after it is stopped. An approval prompt stays on screen for exactly this long — and a call nobody answered by then does not run, so a short wait here is a run that closes on its own rather than one that hangs.
settings.row.subagentsEnabled.desc: Off by default. While it is on, one round per prompt may delegate a self-contained question to a second local model run. That subagent has its own two-request budget, can only read this workspace — four reads, no writes, no shell, no network — and returns one answer as one tool result. One delegation per prompt.
settings.row.compressAt.desc: Share of the model window after which older turns are summarized into a “Context compressed” divider.
settings.row.keepRecentTurns.desc: Recent turns, plus every open file, are kept verbatim.
settings.row.allowRemote.desc: On: a run with tools may search Wikipedia and read one web page back, every lookup stands in the transcript, and the remote provider below may answer. Off: web tools are withheld and a selected remote provider is refused, not rerouted — a free model picked in the composer still answers, because it is not the address below.
settings.row.remoteSource.desc: Free models answer on this Mac's OpenCode service and need no key. Remote sends every prompt to the provider below instead and never falls back; it needs the Privacy switch and a saved key, and without either the run is refused.
settings.row.remoteBaseUrl.desc: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint. HTTPS is required; plain HTTP is allowed only for an address on this machine. The app appends /v1/chat/completions.
settings.row.remoteModel.desc: The model name the provider expects in each request, spelled exactly as its documentation gives it.
settings.row.remoteContext.desc: Tokens the provider accepts. The reply budget is capped at half this window.
settings.row.remoteKey.desc: Stored in the macOS Keychain, not in this file, and read only when a request is sent.
settings.row.githubToken.desc: Stored in the macOS Keychain, never in this file, and read only when the agent opens a pull request. A push needs no token: git uses the credential this machine already holds for the remote.
settings.row.telemetry.desc: Nothing in this build collects or sends usage data, so there is nothing here to switch.
settings.row.dedicatedServerSlots.desc: Run the server with one slot and a bounded prompt cache, so the cache does not thrash across requests.
settings.row.maxTokens.desc: A cap that is too small ends the run mid-thought and yields an empty reply.
settings.row.systemPrompt.desc: The instruction every run starts from.
settings.row.shortcutNewTask.desc: Starts a fresh conversation. It waits while the search panel or another surface is in front of the transcript.
settings.row.shortcutPalette.desc: Searches the conversations this app has filed by what was said in them; the same key closes it.
settings.row.shortcutSettings.desc: Brings this window over whatever page is underneath. With Settings already in front, it does nothing.
settings.row.shortcutTerminal.desc: Shows the commands this task ran and their output, live while one is running. The same key folds it away.
settings.row.shortcutFiles.desc: Shows the project folder in the desktop's file manager. It refuses with the reason when the folder is gone.
settings.row.shortcutBrowser.desc: Shows the in-app browser in the right column, on a blank tab when none is open.
settings.row.shortcutReview.desc: Shows the files this run changed in the right column.
settings.row.shortcutEscape.desc: Closes the nearest thing — a panel, a surface, a step back — and stops the run once nothing is left to close.
settings.row.storageSessions.noDir: This platform gives the app no directory to file conversations in.

settings.help.title: What is running
transcript.plan.title: Plan
transcript.plan.empty: No plan yet. An agent run states one before it starts changing files.
transcript.plan.hint: The run writes this list and ticks a step once its result is checked.
transcript.summary.lineTooLong: line {{line}} alone passes the output cap
notice.effort-not-supported: {{model}} accepts reasoning effort {{accepted}}; the saved choice "{{chosen}}" is not among them, so this server replies at "{{sent}}". Settings › Reasoning can change it.
notice.effort-not-sent: {{model}} answers without a reasoning-effort field, so the saved choice "{{chosen}}" was not sent. No route in this build accepts one.
notice.engine-restarted:
The engine stopped between runs, so it is being started again (restart {{attempt}} of {{max}}). Its last lines:
{{log}}
notice.tool-call-without-tools: The model asked for a tool ({{name}}). This prompt went out without the workspace tools offered, so nothing was read and the answer is from the model alone. Ask again to have the workspace actually looked at.
notice.tool-not-offered: The model asked for {{name}}, which this build does not have. It has four reads of the workspace (read_file, list_dir, glob, grep_search), three reads of the repository (git_status, git_diff, git_log), three writes inside the workspace (write_file, edit_file, apply_patch), and a terminal with run_tests, run_build and run_linter, which run only while terminal access is on — plus web_search and fetch_url while the privacy switch is on.
notice.tool-loop-capped: The model asked for tools {{rounds}} times in a row without answering, so the run stopped there and its last tool result stands. What you see is the beginning of the answer, not the end. Narrower wording usually gets it to answer in one pass.
notice.prompt-too-long: This prompt is {{tokens}} tokens on the server's own count, and the window is {{window}} wide, so the model will not see all of it: it answers from the end of what it was given, with the beginning dropped before it reaches the model. Shorten the message, or raise Context window in Settings if the machine has the room.
notice.context-trimmed: This conversation has outgrown the context window, so the server could not replay all of it: the model answered from the most recent turns, with the earliest ones dropped before it saw them. Start a new task to answer from a clean window, or raise Context window in Settings if the machine has the room.
notice.budget-exhausted: The reply hit its {{maxTokens}} token cap, so it is cut off. Raise Maximum tokens per reply in Settings if the answer needs more room.
notice.not-filed: This conversation was not filed, so it will not be in the sidebar once the window closes: {{why}}
notice.model-takes-no-images: {{model}} publishes no vision projector, so there is no file this app could start it with to make it read pictures — it answers text alone. A picture needs a model whose card ships one, such as Bonsai 2 4B.
notice.projector-absent: {{model}} can read pictures, but {{file}} — the file that makes it able to — is not in this machine's models directory, so this run stopped before the model saw the picture. Downloading this model's weights fetches it.
notice.projector-loading: A picture needs a server that was started with its vision projector, so the engine is being restarted with {{file}} loaded. The wait is the model coming back up, not the answer.
notice.free-model-fallback: {{from}} refused the request before a token landed, so this turn was answered by {{to}} instead. An older build moved a refused free turn between models; this one asks only the model you picked.
notice.route-has-no-tools: {{model}} answers this run through the free-model service, and none of this app's tools go with it: the run's steps never reach this transcript, and anything it writes lands in that service's own folder rather than this one, where Review shows nothing and this window cannot undo it. The loop that works in this folder runs on the local engine or on a provider that takes a key.
notice.checks-not-run: This run changed files, and the project's checks were not run: Terminal access is off in Settings, so this window runs no command. Turn it on to have the tests measured after each change.
notice.checks-unavailable: This run changed files, and the project declares no test, build or lint command at its root, so there was no check to run. The change is unverified.
notice.checks-failed: The project's check failed with exit {{code}}, so this run's change is not verified. The row above holds the command and its output.
notice.instructions-read: This run carries your instructions from {{files}} — {{chars}} characters, read from the folder before the request went out. Where they and this app's own contract disagree about how the work should be done, these are the ones the answer follows.
notice.instructions-cut: {{files}} hold more than the {{chars}} characters the instruction files share, so this run saw only the beginning of them. Shorten the file if a rule in the rest of it has to be honoured.
blocker.engine-not-installed.title: The engine isn't on this machine yet
blocker.engine-not-installed.detail: FreeCode runs models with one specific build of llama.cpp, and this machine doesn't have it yet. Installing it fetches exactly the build this app was pinned to — nothing else is chosen for you.
blocker.stock-engine-rejected.title: This model can't run on standard llama.cpp
blocker.stock-engine-rejected.detail: The llama.cpp on this machine is the standard one, which can't read these weights. Installing the build this app pins is what fixes it; the app will never quietly fall back to a build that answers wrongly.
blocker.weights-not-downloaded.title: The model file hasn't been downloaded yet
blocker.weights-not-downloaded.detail: {{file}} hasn't been downloaded yet, and nothing can run without it.
blocker.integrity-mismatch.title: The model file isn't the one that was published
blocker.integrity-mismatch.detail: {{file}} isn't byte-for-byte the file that was published, so the app won't load it — an interrupted download is the usual cause. Downloading it again clears this.
blocker.rotation-metadata-missing.title: This file wasn't exported by Prism
blocker.rotation-metadata-missing.detail: This file came from somewhere other than the official Prism release, and a ternary model without its rotation settings answers confidently and wrongly rather than failing loudly. Get the file from the model's own page.
blocker.engine-pin-too-old.title: The pinned engine build has no downloadable files
blocker.engine-pin-too-old.detail: The engine build this app is pinned to was published without any files to download, so there is nothing here the app can fetch. Moving the pin to the next build that ships binaries clears this.
sidebar.extensionsAbout: The tools the agent is offered, and which of them this build runs
extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.loadFailed: The tool registry could not be read: {{error}}
extensions.about: This app installs no add-ons, so the row's local meaning is the other thing that lives in that place: the capabilities the model is handed when it is allowed to act.
extensions.runs.desc: {{count}} tools reach an executor: a file call is confined to the workspace root named at the left, a web call leaves the machine only while the privacy switch is on, and every result is replayed into the next request. The two labels on the right are the class of the call, and what the approval dial in force would do with it.
extensions.declaredOnly.desc: {{count}} tools this build declares but has no executor for. They are not in the set a run is offered, so one only appears if the model names it anyway — and then the transcript shows the notice that says so, and stops there.
extensions.note: Both columns are the host's own answer. The classes come from the registry a run is built from, and the right-hand label comes from the policy engine that decides a call mid-run — so this list moves with the approval dial and the privacy switch in Settings, and cannot read more permissive than the agent acts.
modelPicker.freeNoteApp: The next prompt is answered by the free model picked here, through FreeCode on this Mac. No key is used, and the free-model service has to stay running.
model.free.appReady: Prompts are answered by this free model through FreeCode on this Mac: no key is read, and the service's password never leaves the machine. The free-model service has to stay running — a prompt sent after it stops is refused with that reason.
onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to FreeCode
onboarding.welcome.subtitle: Your own coding assistant, running on this Mac.

onboarding.welcome.feature2.title: Answer with what you have
onboarding.welcome.feature2.desc: A free model, a provider you already use, or this Mac's own engine — the route you pick answers every prompt.
onboarding.welcome.feature3.title: Stay in control
onboarding.welcome.feature3.desc: Permissions decide what the agent may touch, and every run says which route answered it.
onboarding.welcome.note: FreeCode can change files in the folder you give it. Review a run's diff before keeping it, and only connect tools you trust.

onboarding.place.folder.chooseTitle: Choose the folder runs work in
onboarding.place.later.title: Decide later
onboarding.place.later.desc: Finish setup now and choose where runs work when you start your first task.

onboarding.model.subtitle: This is the model that answers your first prompt. Every row is free, and the composer's model pill changes it at any time.
onboarding.model.lead: FreeCode answers through the free-model service on this Mac. No key is saved and nothing is installed or downloaded.
